scope: Evidence, construct-selection, cue-operationalisation and validation contract for a future headline recognition stage after preview impression; no executable mechanism or UI.

stage_decision.rationale: The primary Shulman Study 3 recognition experiment tests later recognition of presented headline stimuli and does not require a full-article click/open before the SDT outcome.

selected.label: Recognition sensitivity
basis: The primary mechanism experiment reports signal-detection sensitivity d-prime directly.
The selected construct can be validated against the source result without relabeling an inferred attention mechanism as a direct observable.
limitations: D-prime is a task-level discrimination metric rather than an event-level memory probability.
The source authors interpret d-prime as evidence about attention and retention, but the measure does not uniquely identify visual attention or neural encoding.

deferred.label: Latent attention allocation
basis: Attention is a plausible explanation offered by the primary source.
A later direct-attention study could justify a separate state.
limitations: Study 3 does not directly measure gaze, fixation, dwell time or a unique latent attention state.

deferred.label: Event-level encoding probability
basis: An event-level encoding quantity could eventually connect exposure to later memory.
It would be more suitable for runtime simulation than a group-level d-prime metric if independently justified.
limitations: The primary source does not provide a unique mapping from condition-level d-prime to item-level encoding probability.

selected.label: Headline simplicity condition
selected.divergence_from_source: CBD freezes the experimentally controlled simple-versus-complex condition as metadata instead of reproducing the publication's composite simplicity index or proprietary LIWC-derived components at runtime.

sources.citation: Shulman, H. C., Markowitz, D. M., & Rogers, T. (2024). Reading dies in complexity: Online news consumers prefer simple writing. Science Advances, 10(23), eadn2555. Study 3 general-reader signal-detection experiment.
sources.notes: Preregistered Study 3. General readers showed higher d-prime recognition sensitivity after simpler versus complex headline conditions.

sources.citation: Shulman, H. C., Markowitz, D. M., & Rogers, T. (2024). Reading dies in complexity: Online news consumers prefer simple writing. Science Advances, 10(23), eadn2555. Study 4 professional-writer signal-detection experiment.
sources.notes: Distinct professional-writer sample. The simplicity effect on SDT sensitivity was not significant, so expertise/task orientation is a mandatory boundary condition.

sources.citation: Shulman, H. C., Markowitz, D. M., & Rogers, T. (2024). Reading dies in complexity: Online news consumers prefer simple writing. Science Advances, 10(23), eadn2555. Washington Post field-experiment component.
sources.notes: Field experiments support greater selection of simpler headlines but do not directly measure recognition sensitivity; used only to connect the simplicity cue to the preceding access literature.

sources.citation: Mattis, N., Heitz, L., Masur, P. K., Moeller, J., & van Atteveldt, W. (2025). Nudges for news recommenders: prominent article positioning increases selection, engagement, and recall of environmental news, but reducing complexity does not. Journal of Communication, 75(6), 437-449.
sources.notes: Preregistered seven-day field experiment. Simplifying article text did not significantly improve factual recall, limiting generalization across stimulus levels and contexts.

sources.citation: Robertson, R. E., Green, J., Ruck, D. J., Ognyanova, K., Wilson, C., & Lazer, D. (2023). Users choose to engage with more partisan news than they are exposed to on Google Search. Nature, 618, 342-348.
sources.notes: Separates URLs shown from URLs selected, supporting the distinction between exposure/impression and later engagement. It does not calibrate recognition.

sources.citation: González-Bailón, S., Lazer, D., Barberá, P., et al. (2023). Asymmetric ideological segregation in exposure to political news on Facebook. Science, 381(6656), 392-398.
sources.notes: Separates potential exposure, actual exposure after curation and engagement. Used only for funnel-stage architecture, not recognition calibration.

planned_quantities.definition: Binary controlled headline-simplicity condition reserved for the future M1.E4 reference comparator.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not intelligence, education, source quality, comprehension ability, article truth or article-level difficulty.

planned_quantities.definition: Signal-detection recognition sensitivity d-prime derived from a registered target/foil probe set.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not a directly observed attention state, gaze measure, fixation duration, event-level encoding probability, comprehension or belief.

planned_quantities.definition: Binary response to a recognition probe indicating whether the participant/synthetic agent reports that a phrase was previously present.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not correctness by itself, not belief, and not proof of conscious recollection.

planned_quantities.definition: Registered probe label indicating target versus foil status for computing hit and false-alarm rates.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not truth of the news claim or factuality of the headline.

empirical_target.comparison: simpler versus complex headline condition after registered preview exposure

design.source_note: Study 3 recruited N=524. The published SDT comparison reports t(483)=6.01; CBD does not infer an analyzed-N value beyond what is directly reported.

empirical_target.model_match: A future M1.E4 candidate may use only the directional simpler-Hsimp to higher-Drecog pattern. Published d-prime means and Cohen's d do not set an event-level CBD encoding coefficient.
empirical_target.limitations: Recognition sensitivity is a delayed task-level outcome and cannot uniquely identify attention allocation or an event-level encoding probability. The primary sample is crowdsourced U.S. adults, and the same publication reports a professional-writer null boundary.

boundary_target.comparison: simpler versus complex headline condition among professional writers

planned_patterns.name: Headline-simplicity recognition differential
planned_patterns.pattern: Holding the registered M1.E4 comparator conditions fixed, simpler Hsimp must correspond to higher Drecog than the complex/control condition in the selected general-reader reference target.

planned_patterns.name: Recognition null
planned_patterns.pattern: When Hsimp variation is removed or ignored, otherwise identical conditions must converge in the recognition-sensitivity target.

planned_patterns.name: Recognition sensitivity is not directly observed attention
planned_patterns.pattern: A Drecog difference must not be represented as a directly measured gaze, fixation, dwell-time or unique latent-attention difference.

planned_patterns.name: Recognition is not downstream belief or action
planned_patterns.pattern: A future M1.E4 recognition mechanism must not directly mutate retained M0 belief/Share, M1.E1 Aissue, M1.E2 Pengage/EngageIntent or M1.E3 Access.

planned_patterns.name: Professional-sample boundary
planned_patterns.pattern: Documentation and future implementation must preserve the Shulman Study 4 professional-writer null and must not claim a universal simplicity-to-recognition effect.
